records.Title: LNA-Persona-Founder-Executive
records.Solution__c:
Founder and Executive Persona

 

CEO, Founder, Managing Director at startups and smaller companies.

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Role Definition
Leads the company, often wearing multiple hats. Makes fast decisions with limited resources. Needs to look professional despite small team size.

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Typical Titles
- CEO / Co-CEO
- Founder / Co-Founder
- Managing Director
- President
- Owner

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Responsibilities
- Set company strategy and direction
- Make key business decisions
- Pitch to investors and partners
- Manage limited resources efficiently
- Represent company externally
- Handle multiple functions personally

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Key Pains
- Resource constraints: cannot afford dedicated research. Statista solution: self-serve platform.
- Wearing many hats: no time for deep research. Statista solution: quick answers.
- Need to look credible: competing with larger companies. Statista solution: professional data and charts.
- Fast decision pace: cannot wait for lengthy research. Statista solution: instant access.
- Investor expectations: need market validation. Statista solution: TAM/market sizing data.

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Goals
- Make fast, informed decisions
- Look professional in investor and client meetings
- Validate market assumptions quickly
- Save time on research
- Punch above their weight class

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Buying Behavior
- Decision authority: very high, direct decision maker
- Budget: personal/company decision, often credit card purchase
- Evaluation style: quick evaluation, values simplicity
- Procurement: no formal process, fast decisions

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Product Fit
- Platform (Primary): all-purpose research

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Messaging Approach
Lead with:
- Simplicity: find any stat in seconds
- Credibility: look professional with trusted data
- Efficiency: stop spending hours on Google searches
Avoid:
- Complex enterprise pitches
- Heavy feature lists
- Lengthy evaluation processes

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Objection Patterns
- "I find free data online": likely means cost sensitivity. Response: time savings plus credibility risk of free sources.
- "Too busy to look at this": likely means time pressure. Response: show instant value, minimal time commitment.
- "Not sure it's for my industry": likely means coverage concern. Response: show breadth, relevant examples.

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Discovery Questions
- How do you currently research market data?
- What do you use for investor presentations?
- How much time do you spend on research each week?
- What is your biggest market question right now?
- Do you create pitch decks or client proposals?

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Engagement Tips
- Tone: casual, direct, founder-to-founder style
- Content: quick demo, relevant examples
- Meeting: very short, value-focused
- Follow-up: simple next step, trial access

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Startup Stage Considerations
- Pre-seed/Seed: market validation, pitch deck support
- Series A: TAM/SAM sizing, competitive context
- Series B+: may transition to Strategy Leader persona

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Special Characteristics
Founders often:
- Make fast yes/no decisions
- Value relationship and trust
- Become strong advocates if they love the product
- Have high potential for growth (today's startup is tomorrow's enterprise)
- Connect with other founders (referral potential)

 

Founder and Executive Persona — Summary
Founders lead their companies and make fast decisions with limited resources. They struggle with time constraints and need to look credible despite small team size. Statista fits as a quick, self-serve platform for all-purpose research. Lead with simplicity and credibility, keep engagement short, and recognize their growth potential.

records.Title: LNA-Persona-Marketing-Leader
records.Solution__c:
Marketing Leader Persona

 

CMO, VP Marketing, Marketing Director, Brand Director, Head of Brand Strategy.

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Role Definition
Drives brand strategy, campaign planning, and marketing effectiveness. Needs to understand consumers, justify spend, and demonstrate marketing ROI.

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Typical Titles
- Chief Marketing Officer (CMO)
- VP of Marketing
- Marketing Director
- Brand Director
- Head of Brand Strategy
- VP Consumer Marketing
- Director of Consumer Insights

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Responsibilities
- Develop and execute brand strategy
- Plan and optimize marketing campaigns
- Understand target audiences and consumer behavior
- Justify marketing budget and demonstrate ROI
- Guide creative and messaging direction
- Track brand health and market position

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Key Pains
- Hard to quantify audiences: weak targeting. Statista solution: Consumer Insights data.
- Lack of consumer evidence: gut-feel decisions. Statista solution: behavior and attitude data.
- Justifying marketing spend: budget pressure. Statista solution: data-backed campaign support.
- Disconnected consumer signals: fragmented view. Statista solution: unified consumer platform.
- Outdated research cycles: stale insights. Statista solution: regular Consumer Insights updates.

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Goals
- Build data-backed campaign strategies
- Understand consumers deeply across segments
- Prove marketing effectiveness and ROI
- Stay current on consumer trends
- Inform creative with real insights

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Buying Behavior
- Decision authority: high for marketing tools, may need CMO for larger deals
- Budget: marketing budget, sometimes shared with insights
- Evaluation style: values consumer depth, ease of use, visual outputs
- Procurement: marketing tech stack purchases, may have preferred vendor process

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Product Fit
- Consumer Insights (Primary): audience understanding, attitudes
- Platform (Secondary): general facts, presentations

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Messaging Approach
Lead with:
- Consumer understanding: know your audience beyond demographics
- Campaign support: data-backed creative and targeting
- ROI justification: evidence for marketing effectiveness
Avoid:
- Overly technical data talk
- B2B-heavy positioning
- Complex integration pitches

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Objection Patterns
- "We do our own research": likely means custom surveys. Response: position Statista for broader context and faster cycles.
- "We have Nielsen/Kantar": likely means deep syndicated data. Response: complement with consumer attitudes.
- "Not in budget": likely a cost concern. Response: ROI through efficiency plus existing research complement.

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Discovery Questions
- How do you currently understand your target consumers?
- What data feeds into your campaign planning?
- How do you track changing consumer attitudes?
- What is your biggest consumer insight gap right now?
- How often do you need fresh consumer data?

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Engagement Tips
- Tone: creative-friendly, insight-focused, collaborative
- Content: consumer insight examples, visual outputs, category relevance
- Meeting: show relevant consumer data early, they want to see the product
- Follow-up: send consumer insight sample relevant to their category

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Industry Variations
- FMCG: category behavior, purchase drivers
- Retail: shopper insights, channel preferences
- Tech (B2C): digital behavior, app usage
- Media: audience consumption, content preferences
- Travel: traveler behavior, booking patterns

 

Marketing Leader Persona — Summary
Marketing Leaders drive brand strategy and campaign effectiveness. They need deep consumer understanding to justify spend and improve targeting. They struggle with quantifying audiences and outdated research. Statista fits through Consumer Insights for behavior and attitudes data. Lead with consumer understanding and campaign support, show relevant data early, and connect to their category.

records.Title: LNA-Persona-Executive-Assistant
records.Solution__c:
Executive Assistant Persona

 

EA, Chief of Staff, Executive Support, Office Manager.

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Role Definition
Supports C-level executives with research, scheduling, and administrative tasks. Often a gatekeeper but also an influencer and internal champion. May do research on behalf of executives.

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Typical Titles
- Executive Assistant (EA)
- Chief of Staff
- Executive Coordinator
- Office Manager
- Executive Support

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Responsibilities
- Support executive with research requests
- Prepare meeting materials and briefings
- Manage executive's calendar and priorities
- Screen vendors and requests
- Coordinate with other teams
- Anticipate executive's needs

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Key Pains
- Last-minute research requests: time pressure to deliver fast. Statista solution: quick answers.
- Need to find reliable information: executive credibility at stake. Statista solution: trusted source.
- Multiple topics to research: constant context switching. Statista solution: broad coverage.
- Supporting executive presentations: visual needs. Statista solution: ready-to-use charts.
- Limited research expertise: quality concerns. Statista solution: easy-to-use platform.

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Goals
- Respond quickly to executive requests
- Provide reliable, professional information
- Anticipate executive's research needs
- Make executive look good
- Simplify research process

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Buying Behavior
- Decision authority: low for purchase, high for influence and access
- Budget: executive's budget or departmental
- Evaluation style: ease of use, reliability, executive approval
- Procurement: can recommend, executive decides

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Product Fit
- Platform (Primary): research for executive

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Messaging Approach
Lead with:
- Speed: answer executive requests in minutes
- Reliability: trusted data your executive can rely on
- Ease: simple to use, no expertise required
Avoid:
- Technical complexity
- Long evaluation processes
- Going over their head prematurely

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Engagement Strategy
EAs are unique in the sales process and can serve three roles:

 

As Gatekeeper:
- Respect their role in screening
- Provide clear, concise value proposition
- Offer to share materials they can forward
- Do not try to bypass, work with them

 

As Champion:
- Enable them to recommend internally
- Provide executive-friendly summaries
- Help them look good to their executive
- They can become strong advocates

 

As User:
- They may be primary day-to-day users
- Focus on ease of use and speed
- Show how it helps their specific tasks

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Discovery Questions
- What types of research requests do you handle for your executive?
- How do you typically find information for presentations?
- What topics come up most frequently?
- How quickly do you usually need to turn around research?
- Would it be helpful if I shared some examples you could review?

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Engagement Tips
- Tone: respectful, helpful, professional
- Content: easy-to-share summaries, visual examples
- Meeting: be flexible with scheduling (they manage calendars)
- Follow-up: materials they can easily forward

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Reaching the Executive
EAs can help you reach their executive if you:
- Build trust and credibility first
- Provide value to the EA
- Make it easy for them to recommend
- Respect their assessment of timing
- Do not push them to bypass their role

 

Executive Assistant Persona — Summary
Executive Assistants support C-level executives with research and can be gatekeepers, champions, or users. They need quick, reliable information to support their executive. Statista fits as an easy-to-use platform for research requests. Work with them, not around them. They can become valuable advocates who facilitate executive access.

records.Title: LNA-Persona-Product-Leader
records.Solution__c:
Product Leader Persona

 

CPO, VP Product, Director of Product, Product Manager, Head of Product Strategy.

 

Product Leader Persona — Role Definition
Drives product strategy, roadmap prioritization, and go-to-market decisions. Needs external market context to complement internal product metrics.

 

Product Leader Persona — Typical Titles
- Chief Product Officer (CPO)
- VP of Product
- Director of Product Management
- Senior Product Manager
- Head of Product Strategy
- Product Lead

 

Product Leader Persona — Responsibilities
- Define product strategy and roadmap
- Prioritize features and investments
- Understand market opportunity and competitive landscape
- Guide go-to-market strategy
- Validate product-market fit
- Support board and investor updates with market context

 

Product Leader Persona — Key Pains
- Missing external context: internal-only view limits decisions. Statista solution: market and adoption data.
- Hard to size opportunities: weak prioritization. Statista solution: market sizing and forecasts.
- Limited competitive visibility: blind spots in landscape. Statista solution: industry benchmarks.
- Need to understand verticals: selling to multiple industries is hard. Statista solution: cross-industry coverage.
- TAM validation for investors: credibility gaps in pitches. Statista solution: comparable market data.

 

Product Leader Persona — Goals
- Understand market adoption and trends
- Validate opportunity sizing
- Make data-informed roadmap decisions
- Support investor and board communications
- Stay ahead of competitive landscape

 

Product Leader Persona — Buying Behavior
- Decision authority: high for product tools, moderate for research tools
- Budget: product budget, sometimes shared with strategy
- Evaluation style: values structured data, API potential, efficiency
- Procurement: may prefer self-serve or quick trials

 

Product Leader Persona — Product Fit
- Platform (Primary): quick research, presentations
- Market Insights (Primary): market sizing, forecasts
- Connect/API (Secondary): dashboard integration, AI tools
- Consumer Insights (Varies): B2C product focus

 

Product Leader Persona — Messaging Approach
Lead with:
- External context: market perspective beyond your product metrics
- Opportunity sizing: validate TAM and prioritize with data
- Efficiency: answer market questions without lengthy research
Avoid:
- Heavy enterprise sales approach
- Overly marketing-focused positioning
- Complexity that slows evaluation

 

Product Leader Persona — Objection Patterns
- "We have good internal data": likely means analytics-heavy. Response: position Statista for external market context.
- "We use analysts (Gartner/Forrester)": likely means tech-specific depth. Response: broader market coverage plus consumer data.
- "Not sure it's relevant": likely needs to see value. Response: quick demo with relevant data.

 

Product Leader Persona — Discovery Questions
- How do you currently get external market context for roadmap decisions?
- How do you validate market opportunity for new features or products?
- What industries or verticals are you selling into?
- Do you need market data for investor or board updates?
- How do your product and data teams work together?

 

Product Leader Persona — Engagement Tips
- Tone: direct, efficient, data-focused
- Content: market sizing examples, relevant industry data
- Meeting: get to the data quickly, they want to evaluate relevance
- Follow-up: send specific data relevant to their market

 

Product Leader Persona — Tech Company Considerations
Product leaders at tech companies often:
- Have strong internal analytics (complement with external)
- Need to understand target verticals (multi-industry coverage)
- Think about API integration (mention Connect early)
- Value speed and self-service

 

Product Leader Persona — Summary
Product Leaders drive roadmap decisions and need external market context to complement their internal metrics. They struggle with opportunity sizing and understanding target verticals. Statista fits through Platform and Market Insights for market sizing and industry trends. Lead with external context positioning, be efficient in engagement, and show relevant market data quickly.

records.Title: LNA-Persona-Strategy-Leader
records.Solution__c:
Strategy Leader Persona

 

VP/Director Strategy, Chief Strategy Officer, Head of Corporate Development, Strategic Planning Lead.

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Role Definition
Sets corporate direction, evaluates markets, guides investments, and supports executive decision-making. Often reports to C-suite and prepares materials for board presentations.

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Typical Titles
- VP of Strategy
- Director of Strategy
- Chief Strategy Officer (CSO)
- Head of Corporate Development
- VP Corporate Development
- Director of Strategic Planning
- Head of M&A

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Responsibilities
- Evaluate new markets and expansion opportunities
- Prepare board and executive presentations
- Guide investment decisions and portfolio strategy
- Conduct competitive analysis
- Support M&A due diligence
- Develop long-term strategic plans

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Key Pains
- Slow access to market evidence: delays strategy cycles. Statista solution: fast research across industries.
- Fragmented data sources: inconsistent analysis. Statista solution: unified platform.
- Need executive-ready insights: manual formatting time. Statista solution: ready-to-use charts.
- Inconsistent baselines across teams: conflicting numbers. Statista solution: single source of truth.
- Time pressure on strategy projects: quality vs speed tradeoff. Statista solution: rapid fact-finding.

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Goals
- Make faster, better-informed decisions
- Provide credible fact base for leadership
- Maintain consistent market view across organization
- Reduce time spent on research and formatting
- Look professional and well-prepared in meetings

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Buying Behavior
- Decision authority: high, can approve mid-size purchases, influence larger ones
- Budget: strategy budget or cross-functional allocation
- Evaluation style: values credibility, breadth, and ease of use
- Procurement: may bypass formal procurement for right-priced solutions

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Product Fit
- Platform (Primary): day-to-day research, quick facts
- Market Insights (Primary): market sizing, opportunity assessment
- Connect (Secondary): strategy portals, AI research tools

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Messaging Approach
Lead with:
- Speed: find market evidence in minutes, not days
- Credibility: trusted source for board-level materials
- Efficiency: consistent baselines across your strategy team
Avoid:
- Feature-heavy pitches
- Overly technical positioning
- Price as primary differentiator

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Objection Patterns
- "We use consultants": likely means deep dives are outsourced. Response: position Statista for between-projects agility.
- "We have other sources": likely checking differentiation. Response: position as complement for breadth.
- "Not a priority now": likely a timing issue. Response: connect to upcoming planning cycles.

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Discovery Questions
- How do you currently source market data for strategy materials?
- What is your process for preparing board presentations?
- How consistent is market sizing across your teams?
- When do you typically go through annual planning cycles?
- What markets or topics are hardest to get data on?

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Engagement Tips
- Tone: professional, peer-to-peer, respect their expertise
- Content: case studies from similar companies, sample outputs
- Meeting: they are time-scarce, be concise and value-focused
- Follow-up: send relevant data on topics they mentioned

 

Strategy Leader Persona — Summary
Strategy Leaders are senior decision-makers who set corporate direction and need fast access to credible market evidence. They struggle with slow research cycles and fragmented sources. Statista fits as a unified platform for market data with ready-to-use visuals. Lead with speed and credibility, connect to their planning cycles, and respect their time constraints.

records.Title: LNA-Persona-Consultant
records.Solution__c:
Consultant Persona

 

Partner, Principal, Manager, Consultant, Analyst at consulting firms.

 

Consultant Persona — Role Definition
Delivers client projects across many industries, often with tight timelines. Needs to ramp up quickly on unfamiliar sectors and produce credible deliverables.

 

Consultant Persona — Typical Titles
- Partner / Managing Partner
- Principal
- Director
- Manager / Engagement Manager
- Senior Consultant
- Consultant
- Analyst / Associate

 

Consultant Persona — Responsibilities
- Deliver client engagements across industries
- Produce strategy recommendations
- Create presentation-ready deliverables
- Conduct market research and analysis
- Develop thought leadership content
- Support business development and pitches

 

Consultant Persona — Key Pains
- Rapid ramp-up needs: each project is a new industry. Statista solution: cross-industry coverage.
- Time pressure: tight deadlines on every engagement. Statista solution: fast research.
- Slide-heavy deliverables: manual formatting takes time. Statista solution: ready visuals.
- Cross-country consistency: different data formats across regions. Statista solution: comparable global data.
- Credibility requirements: client expectations are high. Statista solution: sourced, trusted data.

 

Consultant Persona — Goals
- Deliver quality work faster
- Reduce ramp-up time on new sectors
- Create professional deliverables
- Maintain consistency across projects
- Support business development with data

 

Consultant Persona — Buying Behavior
- Decision authority: partners decide firm-wide, managers may have project budgets
- Budget: firm-wide license or project-based
- Evaluation style: values speed, breadth, visual quality
- Procurement: often centralized through knowledge/IT

 

Consultant Persona — Product Fit
- Platform (Primary): daily research, quick facts
- Market Insights (Primary): client market sizing
- Connect (Secondary): knowledge portals

 

Consultant Persona — Messaging Approach
Lead with:
- Speed: cut research time in half
- Breadth: cover any industry your clients need
- Credibility: source-backed data for client deliverables
Avoid:
- Positioning as replacement for deep expertise
- Overly simplistic messaging
- Heavy technical pitches

 

Consultant Persona — Objection Patterns
- "We have internal research": likely means existing knowledge base. Response: complement with external data.
- "Clients provide data": likely means project-specific data. Response: baseline context plus validation.
- "Not sure about coverage": likely means sector concerns. Response: show breadth, acknowledge depth limits.

 

Consultant Persona — Discovery Questions
- How do you currently research industries for new client projects?
- What is your typical turnaround time for market analysis?
- How do you maintain consistency across global projects?
- What industries does your practice focus on?
- Do you use a centralized knowledge management system?

 

Consultant Persona — Engagement Tips
- Tone: peer-to-peer, professional, efficient
- Content: show industry coverage, visual quality
- Meeting: respect their time, get to value quickly
- Follow-up: examples from industries they mentioned

 

Consultant Persona — Seniority Considerations
- Partner: focus on firm-wide value, client impact
- Manager: focus on project efficiency, team enablement
- Consultant/Analyst: focus on daily usage, research speed

 

Consultant Persona — Firm Tier Differences
- MBB (McKinsey, BCG, Bain): enterprise-wide, complex procurement
- Big 4 (Deloitte, PwC, EY, KPMG): multiple practices, decentralized
- Boutique: faster decisions, direct to partners

 

Consultant Persona — Summary
Consultants deliver projects across many industries under tight timelines. They struggle with rapid ramp-up on new sectors and creating consistent deliverables. Statista fits for cross-industry research with ready visuals. Lead with speed and breadth, respect their time, and show industry coverage relevant to their practice.

records.Title: LNA-Persona-Data-BI-Leader
records.Solution__c:
Data and BI Leader Persona

 

CDO, Head of Analytics, BI Manager, VP Data, Data Platform Lead.

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Role Definition
Manages data infrastructure, BI tools, analytics capabilities, and increasingly AI/ML initiatives. Focused on data governance, integration, and enabling data-driven decisions across the organization.

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Typical Titles
- Chief Data Officer (CDO)
- VP of Data
- Head of Analytics
- Director of Business Intelligence
- Data Platform Lead
- Head of Data Engineering
- VP Analytics and Insights

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Responsibilities
- Build and maintain data infrastructure
- Manage BI dashboards and reporting
- Ensure data governance and quality
- Enable AI/ML initiatives with quality data
- Integrate data sources across the organization
- Support business users with data access

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Key Pains
- Manual external data ingestion: time-consuming and error-prone. Statista solution: API/Connect automation.
- Lack of governed external sources: quality and trust issues. Statista solution: curated, sourced data.
- AI needs credible external data: hallucination risk. Statista solution: verified statistics for AI.
- Decentralized research: inconsistency across teams. Statista solution: single external source.
- No clear source attribution: compliance risk. Statista solution: transparent sourcing.

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Goals
- Automate external data flows
- Ensure data governance and quality
- Enable AI tools with trusted data
- Reduce manual research burden on business teams
- Create single source of truth for external data

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Buying Behavior
- Decision authority: high for data tools, influences cross-functional
- Budget: data/IT budget, sometimes enterprise-wide
- Evaluation style: technical, integration-focused, governance-aware
- Procurement: IT/vendor management process, security reviews

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Product Fit
- Connect/API (Primary): integration, automation
- Platform (Secondary): manual research fallback

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Messaging Approach
Lead with:
- Integration: external data API for your data platform
- Governance: governed, sourced external data
- AI enablement: trusted data for AI copilots and assistants
Avoid:
- Marketing-heavy positioning
- Manual research focus
- Overselling breadth without depth discussion

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Objection Patterns
- "We build our own pipelines": likely means DIY preference. Response: faster time-to-value, maintained coverage.
- "Concerned about data quality": likely means governance focus. Response: show source transparency, methodology.
- "Need to evaluate API": likely means technical evaluation. Response: provide sandbox access, documentation.

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Discovery Questions
- How do you currently bring external market data into your systems?
- What BI tools or data platforms are you using?
- Are you building AI assistants that need external data?
- How do you ensure data quality for external sources?
- Who else in the organization needs access to this data?

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Connect-Specific Discovery
When AI platform signals are present, add these questions to qualify for Connect:
- Which AI platform is deployed — Copilot, Langdock, Claude, or something else?
- Is it used for research workflows where market data matters?
- How broadly is it rolled out — company-wide, department, or individual?
- Who manages the AI platform technically, and who drives adoption?
- Have you connected any external data sources to your AI tools yet?
- How has your team's usage of Statista.com changed since AI adoption?

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Engagement Tips
- Tone: technical, peer-to-peer, respect their expertise
- Content: API documentation, integration examples, data methodology
- Meeting: be prepared for technical questions, involve SE if needed
- Follow-up: sandbox access, technical documentation

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Technical Considerations
Data/BI leaders care about:
- API capabilities: rate limits, endpoints, formats
- Data freshness: update frequency, versioning
- Authentication: SSO, security standards
- Schema: data structure, consistency
- SLAs: uptime, support response

 

Data and BI Leader Persona — Summary
Data and BI Leaders manage data infrastructure and are focused on governance and integration. They struggle with manual external data ingestion and AI data quality. Statista fits through Connect/API for automated, governed external data. Lead with integration and governance messaging, be prepared for technical evaluation, and involve solutions engineering for complex deals.

records.Title: LNA-ICP-Manufacturing
records.Solution__c:
Industrial & Manufacturing ICP

 

B2B producers with global supply chains and long planning cycles.

 

Industrial & Manufacturing ICP — Identification Signals
- Multi-country manufacturing operations
- Engineering-heavy workforce
- Sustainability and automation initiatives
- Long product development and planning cycles
- B2B sales model (selling to other businesses)

 

Industrial & Manufacturing ICP — Key Pains
- Need sector and tech trend visibility: what is happening in their end markets
- Hard to track global demand shifts: supply chain disruptions, regional variations
- Long planning horizons: need forward-looking data for CapEx decisions
- Sustainability reporting: ESG data requirements increasing
- Technology adoption curves: when to invest in automation, electrification

 

Industrial & Manufacturing ICP — Why Statista Fits
- Industry and technology trends across sectors
- Market sizing for key end-markets
- Comparable data across countries for global operations
- Sustainability and environmental data

 

Industrial & Manufacturing ICP — Product Relevance
- Platform (Primary fit): general research, industry trends
- Market Insights (Primary fit): sector sizing, demand forecasts
- Connect (Secondary fit): BI enrichment, internal dashboards

 

Industrial & Manufacturing ICP — Target Personas
- Strategy Lead: planning, market assessment
- Market Intelligence: competitive analysis, trends
- Innovation Lead: technology adoption, R&D priorities
- Sustainability Lead: ESG reporting, environmental data

 

Industrial & Manufacturing ICP — Sub-Segments
- Automotive: EV transition, supplier trends
- Aerospace & Defense: long cycles, regulatory
- Chemicals: commodity trends, sustainability
- Machinery: automation, end-market demand
- Logistics: volume trends, capacity data

 

Industrial & Manufacturing ICP — Competitive Landscape
Industrial companies typically use industry associations for sector data, specialized consultants for deep dives, trade publications, and internal market research. Statista's angle is breadth across end-markets combined with technology trends and ease of use, providing context beyond their specific sector.

 

Industrial & Manufacturing ICP — Expansion Signals
- Sustainability initiative announced
- Digital transformation or Industry 4.0 program
- Geographic expansion
- New product development in emerging sectors
- M&A activity

 

Industrial & Manufacturing ICP — Summary
Industrial and manufacturing companies need visibility into sector trends and global demand shifts for long-term planning. They struggle with tracking multiple end-markets and sustainability reporting. Statista fits for industry trends, market sizing, and cross-country comparisons. Primary products are Platform and Market Insights. Target personas are Strategy, Market Intelligence, Innovation, and Sustainability Leaders.
